topics.title: Words for reading and analysis
topics.hook: Writers imply, readers infer. These are the words for explaining how a text works.
topics.teach: Use one of today’s words in a sentence about something you’re reading.
topics.talk: Use one of her new words at dinner and see if she notices.

topics.title: Words for thinking and arguing
topics.hook: Point, reason, evidence: these words turn an opinion into an argument.
topics.teach: Use one of today’s words in a sentence about something you’re reading.
topics.talk: Use one of her new words at dinner and see if she notices.

items.prompt: Which word means “to work something out from clues rather than being told directly”?
items.explain: **infer**: to work something out from clues rather than being told directly. Example: From his muddy boots, we can infer that he walked across the field.
items.learn:
**infer** means to work something out from clues rather than being told directly.

_From his muddy boots, we can infer that he walked across the field._
items.hook: Writers imply, readers infer: you work it out from the clues.
items.example: Wet umbrellas by the door: you can infer it’s raining outside.

items.prompt: Which word means “to suggest something without saying it directly”?
items.explain: **imply**: to suggest something without saying it directly. Example: The writer implies that the house is haunted.
items.learn:
**imply** means to suggest something without saying it directly.

_The writer implies that the house is haunted._
items.hook: Imply = put the meaning IN without saying it. The reader then infers it.
items.example: A sign saying “Smile, you’re on CCTV” implies you are being watched.

items.prompt: Which word means “to communicate an idea or feeling”?
items.explain: **convey**: to communicate an idea or feeling. Example: The dark colours convey a gloomy mood.
items.learn:
**convey** means to communicate an idea or feeling.

_The dark colours convey a gloomy mood._
items.hook: Like a conveyor belt, words convey (carry) an idea to the reader.

items.prompt: Which word means “to examine something in detail to understand it”?
items.explain: **analyse**: to examine something in detail to understand it. Example: Analyse how the poet creates tension.
items.learn:
**analyse** means to examine something in detail to understand it.

_Analyse how the poet creates tension._
items.hook: Analyse = take it apart to see how it works, like a mechanic with an engine.

items.prompt: Which word means “to explain what you think something means”?
items.explain: **interpret**: to explain what you think something means. Example: Readers interpret the ending in different ways.
items.learn:
**interpret** means to explain what you think something means.

_Readers interpret the ending in different ways._
items.example: An interpreter explains what someone means in another language. When you interpret, you explain what a text means.

items.prompt: Which word means “facts or quotations that support an idea”?
items.explain: **evidence**: facts or quotations that support an idea. Example: Use evidence from the text to back up your point.
items.learn:
**evidence** means facts or quotations that support an idea.

_Use evidence from the text to back up your point._
items.hook: Evidence makes your point evident: proof you can point to.

items.prompt: Which word means “stated clearly and directly”?
items.explain: **explicit**: stated clearly and directly. Example: The rules are explicit: no phones in class.
items.learn:
**explicit** means stated clearly and directly.

_The rules are explicit: no phones in class._
items.hook: EXplicit is EXpressed out loud; IMplicit is IMplied (hidden IN).
items.example: “No dogs allowed” on a park gate is explicit.

items.prompt: Which word means “suggested but not stated directly”?
items.explain: **implicit**: suggested but not stated directly. Example: There is an implicit threat in her words.
items.learn:
**implicit** means suggested but not stated directly.

_There is an implicit threat in her words._
items.hook: IMplicit is hidden IN the words; EXplicit is EXpressed openly.

items.prompt: Which word means “the mood or feeling of a place in a story”?
items.explain: **atmosphere**: the mood or feeling of a place in a story. Example: The fog creates a tense atmosphere.
items.learn:
**atmosphere** means the mood or feeling of a place in a story.

_The fog creates a tense atmosphere._
items.example: A ghost-train ride uses dim lights, creaks and screams to build a spooky atmosphere.

items.prompt: Which word means “the attitude or feeling in a piece of writing”?
items.explain: **tone**: the attitude or feeling in a piece of writing. Example: The tone of the letter is angry.
items.learn:
**tone** means the attitude or feeling in a piece of writing.

_The tone of the letter is angry._
items.hook: Tone is the writer’s tone of voice: angry, cheerful, sarcastic, worried…

items.prompt: Which word means “a big idea that a story explores”?
items.explain: **theme**: a big idea that a story explores. Example: Friendship is a theme in the novel.
items.learn:
**theme** means a big idea that a story explores.

_Friendship is a theme in the novel._
items.hook: The plot is what happens; the theme is what it is really ABOUT (friendship, greed, courage).

items.prompt: Which word means “a particular point of view”?
items.explain: **perspective**: a particular point of view. Example: The story is told from the dog’s perspective.
items.learn:
**perspective** means a particular point of view.

_The story is told from the dog’s perspective._
items.example: A football match looks very different from the goalkeeper’s perspective than from the stands.

items.prompt: Which word means “a clear difference between two things placed side by side”?
items.explain: **contrast**: a clear difference between two things placed side by side. Example: The poet contrasts the busy city with the quiet countryside.
items.learn:
**contrast** means a clear difference between two things placed side by side.

_The poet contrasts the busy city with the quiet countryside._

items.prompt: Which word means “to give special importance to something”?
items.explain: **emphasise**: to give special importance to something. Example: The short sentence emphasises her shock.
items.learn:
**emphasise** means to give special importance to something.

_The short sentence emphasises her shock._

items.prompt: Which word means “the way a text is organised and put together”?
items.explain: **structure**: the way a text is organised and put together. Example: The structure moves from past to present.
items.learn:
**structure** means the way a text is organised and put together.

_The structure moves from past to present._
items.hook: struct = build: the structure is how the text is built.

items.prompt: Which word means “to give the main points briefly”?
items.explain: **summarise**: to give the main points briefly. Example: Summarise the chapter in three sentences.
items.learn:
**summarise** means to give the main points briefly.

_Summarise the chapter in three sentences._
items.hook: Summarise = add up the main points into a short SUM.
items.example: The blurb on the back of a book summarises the story without giving away the ending.

items.prompt: Which word means “how important something is and why”?
items.explain: **significance**: how important something is and why. Example: Explain the significance of the Battle of Hastings.
items.learn:
**significance** means how important something is and why.

_Explain the significance of the Battle of Hastings._

items.prompt: Which word means “a result or effect of an action”?
items.explain: **consequence**: a result or effect of an action. Example: One consequence of the flood was that crops were ruined.
items.learn:
**consequence** means a result or effect of an action.

_One consequence of the flood was that crops were ruined._
items.example: Forget your PE kit and the consequence is sitting out the lesson.

items.prompt: Which word means “to judge how good, important or true something is”?
items.explain: **evaluate**: to judge how good, important or true something is. Example: Evaluate how far the plan succeeded.
items.learn:
**evaluate** means to judge how good, important or true something is.

_Evaluate how far the plan succeeded._
items.hook: Evaluate has VALUe inside: judge what it is worth.

items.prompt: Which word means “to give reasons for a decision or opinion”?
items.explain: **justify**: to give reasons for a decision or opinion. Example: Justify your answer with evidence.
items.learn:
**justify** means to give reasons for a decision or opinion.

_Justify your answer with evidence._
items.hook: Justify = give your reasons. “Just because” is not enough!

items.prompt: Which word means “to reach a final decision after thinking”?
items.explain: **conclude**: to reach a final decision after thinking. Example: We can conclude that the plant needs light.
items.learn:
**conclude** means to reach a final decision after thinking.

_We can conclude that the plant needs light._

items.prompt: Which word means “one of several things that cause a result”?
items.explain: **factor**: one of several things that cause a result. Example: Weather was one factor in the defeat.
items.learn:
**factor** means one of several things that cause a result.

_Weather was one factor in the defeat._
items.example: Weather, injuries and luck are all factors in which team wins a match.

items.prompt: Which word means “able to be trusted”?
items.explain: **reliable**: able to be trusted. Example: Is this source reliable?
items.learn:
**reliable** means able to be trusted.

_Is this source reliable?_
items.hook: Reliable: something you can RELY on.

items.prompt: Which word means “an unfair preference for one side”?
items.explain: **bias**: an unfair preference for one side. Example: The report shows bias towards the home team.
items.learn:
**bias** means an unfair preference for one side.

_The report shows bias towards the home team._
items.example: A commentator who only ever praises the home team shows bias.

items.prompt: Which word means “the situation or background that helps explain something”?
items.explain: **context**: the situation or background that helps explain something. Example: In the context of the war, food was scarce.
items.learn:
**context** means the situation or background that helps explain something.

_In the context of the war, food was scarce._
items.example: “Brilliant!” can be praise or sarcasm: only the context tells you which.

items.prompt: Which word means “an idea that can be tested by an experiment”?
items.explain: **hypothesis**: an idea that can be tested by an experiment. Example: My hypothesis is that warm water dissolves sugar faster.
items.learn:
**hypothesis** means an idea that can be tested by an experiment.

_My hypothesis is that warm water dissolves sugar faster._
items.hook: A hypothesis is an educated guess you can test.
items.example: “I think the heavier ball will roll further” is a hypothesis you can test in the playground.

items.prompt: Which word means “correct and exact”?
items.explain: **accurate**: correct and exact. Example: Make accurate measurements with the ruler.
items.learn:
**accurate** means correct and exact.

_Make accurate measurements with the ruler._

items.prompt: Which word means “a strong effect on something”?
items.explain: **impact**: a strong effect on something. Example: The railway had a huge impact on towns.
items.learn:
**impact** means a strong effect on something.

_The railway had a huge impact on towns._
items.example: A meteorite’s impact left a giant crater in Arizona.

items.prompt: Which word means “to look at how things are similar and different”?
items.explain: **compare**: to look at how things are similar and different. Example: Compare the two poems.
items.learn:
**compare** means to look at how things are similar and different.

_Compare the two poems._
items.hook: Compare = similarities AND differences; contrast = differences only.

items.prompt: Which word means “to give reasons why something is true”?
items.explain: **argue**: to give reasons why something is true. Example: Some historians argue that the Normans brought great change.
items.learn:
**argue** means to give reasons why something is true.

_Some historians argue that the Normans brought great change._
